'''Jan Willem Nienhuys''' (born 16 April 1942) is a Dutch mathematician, book translator and [[scientific skepticism|skeptic]]. He taught mathematics at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]]. He is also a board member and secretary of [[Stichting Skepsis]] and an editor of its magazine ''[[Skepter]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.skepsis.nl/skepter.html |title=Skepter: een tijdschrift over pseudowetenschap |publisher=[[Stichting Skepsis]] |access-date=14 January 2015 |language=nl}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Nienhuys studied mathematics in the Netherlands, and in 1966/67 at [[Tulane University]] in [[New Orleans]], where he met his future wife. On 14 September 1970, he earned his [[doctorate]] in mathematics at [[Utrecht University]] under guidance of his promotor [[Hans Freudenthal]].<ref>{{aut|J.W. Nienhuys}}, [http://library.tue.nl/catalog/FullBB.csp?WebAction=ShowFullBB&RequestId=78736266_1&Profile=Default&OpacLanguage=eng&NumberToRetrieve=50&StartValue=16&WebPageNr=1&SearchTerm1=.6.106742&SearchT1=&Index1=Index14&SearchMethod=Find_1&ItemNr=16 Not locally compact monothetic groups] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715001138/http://library.tue.nl/catalog/FullBB.csp?WebAction=ShowFullBB&RequestId=78736266_1&Profile=Default&OpacLanguage=eng&NumberToRetrieve=50&StartValue=16&WebPageNr=1&SearchTerm1=.6.106742&SearchT1=&Index1=Index14&SearchMethod=Find_1&ItemNr=16 |date=2014-07-15 }}. Henkes Holland (1970)</ref> His dissertation was published the same year in the journal ''[[Indagationes Mathematicae]] (Proceedings)''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nienhuys |first=J.W. |date=1970 |title=Not locally compact monothetic groups. II |journal=Indagationes Mathematicae (Proceedings) |publisher=Elsevier |volume=73 |pages=311–326 |doi=10.1016/S1385-7258(70)80036-1 |doi-access=free }}</ref> He then taught mathematics for two years at the [[National Taiwan University]] in [[Taipei]], [[Taiwan]]. Since 1973, Nienhuys taught mathematics at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]]. He also assisted several writers in completing their books, and translated books to [[Dutch language|Dutch]].

Nienhuys married and had two sons with Cheng Shan-Hwei. Born in [[Sichuan]] during the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], she was raised in Taiwan where she also studied mathematics, finishing her studies in the United States. She went on to teach informatics at the [[Erasmus University Rotterdam]] and become the director of the Chinese School Eindhoven. The couple published an article together in 1979, ''Onwaar versus onzinnig'' in the Dutch journal ''Euclides'', and co-authored a book about China, ''China: Geschiedenis, Cultuur, Wetenschap, Kunst En Politiek'' (2007).<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.volkskrant.nl/wca_item/boeken_detail/453/132296/China.html |title=China: geschiedenis, cultuur, wetenschap, kunst en politiek |work=[[de Volkskrant]] |date=2007 |access-date=11 June 2014 |language=nl}}</ref>

== Skepticism ==
Nienhuys is a prolific skeptic. Amongst other things he has written several articles on [[pseudoscience]], mainly about [[quackery]] such as [[homeopathy]] and the [[Vaccine controversies|anti-vaccination movement]]. Since the late 1980s he has served as a board member, and since 2003 secretary of, [[Stichting Skepsis]]. Nienhuys also writes articles as an editorial staff member of the magazine ''[[Skepter]]''. From July 2008 until 6 November 2010, he was editor-in-chief of the [[Vereniging tegen de Kwakzalverij]] website.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Renckens |first=C.N.M. |date=2011 |title=Jan Willem Nienhuys gestopt als webmaster |journal=Nederlands Tijdschrift Tegen de Kwakzalverij |publisher=Vereniging tegen de Kwakzalverij |volume=122 |issue=1 |pages=16–18 |language=nl}}</ref>

In 1983, Nienhuys criticised the confluence model of [[Robert Zajonc|Robert B. Zajonc]] and Gregory B. Markus. This mathematical model would serve as proof that a connection existed between the order of birth and intelligence to the advantage of the firstborn, as Lillian Belmont and Francis A. Marolla concluded in 1973 from a registration of the [[Armed forces of the Netherlands|Dutch armed forces]]. This record consisted of the data of nearly 400,000 19-year-old men born in the period 1944–1947, originally collected to investigate the effects of the [[Dutch famine of 1944|Hunger Winter]] (1944–1945) on mental and physical development.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Belmont |first1=Lillian |last2=Marolla |first2=Francis A. |date=14 December 1973 |title=Birth Order, Family Size, and Intelligence |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=182 |issue=4117 |pages=1096–1101 |doi=10.1126/science.182.4117.1096 |pmid=4750607|bibcode=1973Sci...182.1096B |s2cid=46494586 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://scienceblogs.com/cognitivedaily/2006/02/06/dont-believe-your-big-siblings/ |title=Don't believe your big siblings when they tell you they're naturally smarter |author=Dave Munger |work=[[ScienceBlogs]] |date=6 February 2006 |access-date=15 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Somit |first1=Albert |last2=Arwine |first2=Alan |last3=Peterson |first3=Steven A. |date=1996 |title=Birth Order and Political Behavior |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0KZ3nFptJk0C&pg=PA112 |publisher=University Press of America |page=112 |isbn=0761801340 |access-date=15 January 2015}}</ref> According to Nienhuys, Zajonc and Markus's model contained errors in the logic, calculations and methodology used.<ref>{{aut|J.W. Nienhuys}}, [http://repository.tue.nl/696974 Intelligence models for the Dutch Raven Data] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714125626/http://repository.tue.nl/696974 |date=2014-07-14 }}. Eindhoven University of Technology, 1983</ref>

Since 2010, Nienhuys has been a fellow of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theradicalhumanist.com/index.php?option=com_radical&controller=news&cid=94&Itemid=55 |title=Sixteen Notable Figures in Science and Skepticism Elected CSI Fellows |work=The Radical Humanist |date=13 January 2010 |access-date=15 January 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140623200043/http://www.theradicalhumanist.com/index.php?option=com_radical&controller=news&cid=94&Itemid=55 |archive-date=23 June 2014 }}</ref> He often lectures at [[list of skeptical conferences|skeptical conferences]] such as Skepsis congresses and [[SKEPP]] conventions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://kloptdatwel.nl/2011/01/15/2e-spreker-skepsis-congres-2010-jan-willem-nienhuys/ |title=2e spreker Skepsis-congres 2010: Jan Willem Nienhuys |author=Jan van der Gaag |work=KloptDatWel.nl |publisher=Stichting Skepsis |date=15 January 2011 |access-date=15 January 2015 |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kritischdenken.info/betreffende-betz-3/ |title=Betreffende Betz (3) |author=Jozef Van Giel |work=Kritisch Denken |publisher=Russells Theepot |date=15 June 2014 |access-date=15 January 2015 |language=nl}}</ref> On 4 October 2014, Nienhuys received the Gebroeders Bruinsma Erepenning, an award of the Vereniging tegen de Kwakzalverij.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bnr.nl/nieuws/548808-1409/alternatieve-artsen-vooral-onder-de-indruk-van-eigen-ervaringen |title=Alternatieve artsen vooral onder de indruk van eigen ervaringen |author=Marjan van den Berg |work=[[BNR Newsradio]] |date=30 September 2014 |access-date=15 January 2015 |language=nl}}</ref> The society praised Nienhuys for his "enormous engagement, an amazing ability to quickly master certain issues, an enormous productivity and an unparalleled accuracy."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kwakzalverij.nl/1684/Prijs_voor_bestrijding_kwakzalverij_naar_dr_Jan_Willem_Nienhuys |title=Prijs voor bestrijding kwakzalverij naar dr. Jan Willem Nienhuys |work=Kwakzalverij.nl |publisher=Vereniging tegen de Kwakzalverij |date=27 September 2014 |access-date=15 January 2015 |language=nl}}</ref>

== Works ==
;Author
* ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=AsXUY604pewC&pg De Bruijn's combinatorics: Classroom notes]'' (2011).

;Co-author
* ''China: Geschiedenis, Cultuur, Wetenschap, Kunst En Politiek'' (2007), with Shan-Hwei Nienhuys-Cheng. {{ISBN|9085710219}};
* ''Tussen Waarheid en Waanzin: een Encyclopedie der Pseudo-Wetenschappen'' (1997), with Marcel Hulspas. {{ISBN|9789044502787}};
* ''Discrete wiskunde'' (1991), with [[J. H. van Lint|Jack H. van Lint]]. {{ISBN|9062333680}};
* ''Programmeren met Pascal'' (1988), with Shan-Hwei Nienhuys-Cheng. {{ISBN|9789062333202}}.

;Contributions
* ''Leugens over Louwes: Deventer moordzaak'' (2011), Ton Derksen. {{ISBN|9789491224119}};
* ''The Mars Effect: A French test of over 1 000 sports champions'' (1996), Claude Benski et al. {{ISBN|9780879759889}}.

;Translations
Nienhuys has translated many popular science books to Dutch, including:
* ''Poincaré: wiskundige en filosoof'' (2013), [[Umberto Bottazzini]]. {{ISBN|9789085714095}};
* ''Turing: bouwer van de eerste computers'' (2010), Jean Lassègue. {{ISBN|9789085712893}};
* ''De Natuurwetten: van Archimedes tot Hawking'' (2010), [[Clifford A. Pickover]]. {{ISBN|9789085712947}};
* ''Wetenschap en Islam: Verslag Van Een Vergeten Bloeiperiode'' (2009), [[Ehsan Masood]]. {{ISBN|9789085712855}}.
